=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/resolve_integration_ref.sh:100-101 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The shell resolver accepts a triage issue whose first line is an `origin-pr` marker but lacks an `<!-- check-failure-triage:fp=... -->` fingerprint marker on line 0. When `sed -n '2s/...'` returns empty (no origin marker on line 2) AND the body does not start with `<!-- check-failure-triage:fp=`, the script falls through to `printf '\n'; return 0` (legacy empty result). The Python `resolve_integration_ref` in `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:2885-2888` instead raises `OrchestrateError("malformed triage origin header")` on the same body when `"check-failure-triage:origin-pr=" in child_body` is true.
  WHY: When an attacker authors a triage issue whose body begins with `<!-- check-failure-triage:origin-pr=N base=attacker/branch -->` (no FP marker), the orchestrator shell code path (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` source path through `resolve_integration_ref.sh`) accepts it as legacy and falls back to the default branch, while the Python code path raises. Downstream security-follow-up dispatch inherits whichever base the resolver returned, so the spoofed marker is silently dropped or honored depending on the call site.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:2897-2904 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: When `extract_integration_branch` returns a non-empty `declared_base` AND it differs from `origin_base`, the orchestrator raises `IntegrationBranchMissingError("triage origin PR base mismatch")`. But `declared_base` is computed by `extract_integration_branch`, which now filters to authoritative lines (preamble + orchestrator metadata footer). For a triage body whose preamble happens to declare the same branch as the legitimate orchestrator's footer (e.g. `Integration branch: \`orchestrator/project-249\`` in a triage issue about project 249), and whose origin marker points to `attacker/branch`, the check still raises. The companion case where the preamble intentionally differs to escalate detection works, but there is no explicit test that proves the (declared_base and declared_base != origin_base) clause is reachable AND that it produces a meaningful `IntegrationBranchMissingError` that gets logged with the source-PR reference for triage audit. Without an integration test pinning that the misleading preamble case aborts before the API call is made (or the audit properly distinguishes the cases), the parser could silently regress.
  WHY: If `declared_base` returns a value that differs from the marker in a way that bypasses the `extract_integration_branch` filter (for example, a future change that re-introduces line-permissive parsing to recover legacy behavior), the triage issue could be redirected to `declared_base` without ever consulting the origin PR.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:545-553 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The branch-head read and moved-target short-circuit now run BEFORE the `conclusion != "success"` check. When an audit run failed for an infrastructure reason (missing secret, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `startup_failure`) AND the project branch has advanced since dispatch, the function returns `state: moved-target` with `observed_sha` instead of `state: failed`.
  WHY: On a project whose head is actively moving, repeated `conclusion=failure + branch advanced` will keep returning `moved-target` and the security cycle cap (`MAX_SECURITY_PASS_CYCLES`, default 5) will burn down without ever surfacing the infrastructure failure to the human. The current test exercises `conclusion=failure + branch moved => moved-target`, locking in this behavior.
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:176-183, 184-187 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new identity gate runs BEFORE the fork skip and uses an unguarded `[ "${HEAD_REPO_FULL_NAME}" != "${REPO}" ]` test. Any PR with `HEAD_REPO_FULL_NAME` empty OR pointing to a fork now hard-fails the workflow with `exit 1` and `log "error pr_identity_or_base_unverified pr=${PR_NUMBER}"`, whereas the previous behavior soft-skipped fork PRs with `exit 0` (`skip reason=fork_pr ...`). The fork-skip branch below is now dead code because the identity gate has already failed the run.
  WHY: A maintainer-driven fork PR (e.g. an external contributor opening a `fork:fix` branch off `main` and pushing commits to iterate on CI fixes) will trigger `check_failure_triage.yml` on every CI red. Each run will now `exit 1` and emit a `::error::` line, failing the gate and producing a noisy red X on otherwise-acceptable work. There is no test asserting this is the intended behavior, and no consumer doc explains why a fork-PR red is now a hard failure instead of a soft skip.
